pistacho.title: No-bake pistachio and chocolate cheesecake cups
pistacho.summary: Biscuit crumbs, a soft cream cheese and pure pistachio filling, and a thin chocolate topping make six spoonable desserts. Prepare them ahead and chill for at least four hours.
pistacho.notes: Use unsweetened 100% pistachio paste, not sweet pistachio spread. These are soft desserts served in glasses, not a cheesecake for unmoulding. Refrigerate covered at 4 °C or below for up to 2 days. Contains milk, pistachios and wheat; check the chocolate label too. This editorial formulation has not been physically kitchen-tested.
steps: Prepare the glasses
Set out six 200 ml glasses. Crush 120 g biscuits into fine crumbs.
Make the bases
Melt 40 g butter and mix with the crumbs. Divide between the glasses, press lightly with a spoon and refrigerate.
Mix cheese and pistachio
Briefly beat 300 g cream cheese with 90 g pistachio paste and 45 g icing sugar until smooth. Do not warm the mixture.
Whip the cream
Reserve 60 g cream for the topping. Whip the remaining 140 g cold cream to soft peaks.
Fill the glasses
Fold the whipped cream into the pistachio mixture in two additions. Spoon over the biscuit bases and level the tops.
Make the chocolate topping
Heat the reserved 60 g cream until steaming gently. Pour over 90 g chopped chocolate, wait 2 minutes and stir until smooth.
Top and chill
Let the chocolate cool until barely warm and still fluid. Spread a thin layer over each cup, cover without touching the surface and refrigerate for at least 4 hours.
Finish and serve
Divide 20 g chopped pistachios between the six cups. Serve cold, with the biscuit, pale green filling and chocolate layers visible.
faq: Can I use sweet pistachio spread?
The recipe uses 100% pistachio paste. Sweet spread changes the sweetness and firmness and is not a direct replacement.
Does it need gelatine?
No. The filling stays soft and is eaten with a spoon from the glass.
Can I make it ahead?
Yes. Keep covered at 4 °C or below for up to 2 days and add the chopped pistachios just before serving.

arbol.title: Pesto and cheese puff pastry Christmas tree
arbol.summary: Two sheets of puff pastry enclose basil pesto, mozzarella and Parmesan. Twist the side strips into branches for a warm Christmas centrepiece to share.
arbol.notes: Keep the pastry cold and use thick pesto. Leave the centre spine intact. Bake and serve every offcut: the yield and nutrition include all the pastry and filling. The calculation includes a whole brushing egg even if some is left. Contains wheat, milk, egg and any nuts in the pesto. Refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours, keep up to 2 days and reheat in the oven.
ingredients: chilled rectangular puff pastry, two sheets about 25 × 35 cm
steps: Prepare the pastry
Heat the oven to 200 °C, conventional heat. Put one sheet of pastry, about 25 × 35 cm, on baking parchment on a tray.
Spread the filling
Spread over 80 g pesto, leaving a 1 cm border. Scatter over 100 g mozzarella and 25 g Parmesan.
Cover and chill
Lay the second sheet on top and press gently. Refrigerate for 15 minutes so the pastry is cold for cutting.
Cut the tree
Cut a tall triangle with a small trunk at the bottom. Keep all the offcuts to bake alongside, using another tray if needed.
Cut the branches
Make horizontal cuts every 2 cm on both sides, leaving an uncut centre spine about 3 cm wide. Do not cut the trunk.
Twist and brush
Twist each side strip once or twice without detaching it. Brush the tree and the offcuts with beaten egg.
Bake until golden
Bake for 20–25 minutes until risen, golden and cooked underneath. Smaller offcuts may be ready earlier; remove them when golden.
Serve to share
Rest for 5 minutes, then move the tree onto a board. Serve warm with all the baked offcuts, divided between eight people.
faq: Can I shape it ahead?
Yes. Cover the unbaked tree and refrigerate for up to 12 hours. Brush with egg and bake before serving.
Why chill before cutting?
Cold pastry holds its layers and is easier to twist without distorting the branches.
What happens to the offcuts?
Bake them as snacks. The yield and nutrition count all the pastry and filling, with nothing discarded.
arbol.serving_size: 1/8 of the tree and baked offcuts

brie.title: Cranberry and brie puff pastry bites
brie.summary: Twelve little pastry cups hold melted brie, thick cranberry sauce and walnuts. Bake them in a standard muffin tin for an easy sweet and savoury party appetiser.
brie.notes: Use thick red cranberry sauce, not fresh blueberries. A 24 × 32 cm sheet makes twelve 8 cm squares without waste. Use a metal tin for 12 standard muffins and avoid overfilling. Contains wheat, milk and walnuts. Refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours for up to 2 days, then reheat in the oven. Baking time depends on the pastry and tin.
ingredients: chilled rectangular puff pastry, about 24 × 32 cm
steps: Prepare the tin
Heat the conventional oven to 200 °C. Lightly grease a metal 12-hole standard muffin tin with 5 g oil.
Cut the squares
Unroll 250 g cold pastry into a rectangle about 24 × 32 cm. Cut a 3 × 4 grid to make twelve 8 cm squares.
Line the holes
Press one square gently into each hole, leaving the corners pointing upwards.
Add the brie
Cut 180 g brie into twelve equal pieces of about 15 g. Put one in each pastry cup; the edible rind can stay.
Add cranberry sauce
Spoon 10 g thick cranberry sauce over the brie in each cup. Do not fill the holes to the brim.
Add walnuts
Divide 30 g chopped walnuts and 2 g chopped rosemary leaves between the cups.
Bake the cups
Bake for 18–20 minutes until the edges are golden and the bases cooked. Cover loosely with foil near the end if the tops brown too quickly.
Unmould and serve
Wait 5 minutes before lifting the bites out with a small spoon. Serve two warm bites per person; the melted cheese will be hot.
faq: Are these made with blueberries?
No. Use red cranberries in a thick sauce or preserve; blueberries make a different recipe.
Must I remove the brie rind?
No. The rind is edible and helps contain the cheese. Remove it only if you prefer.
Can I leave out the walnuts?
Yes. Omit them for a nut-free adaptation and check every label. The published nutrition includes the walnuts.

turron.title: Almond turrón tiramisu cups without raw egg
turron.summary: This Christmas variation layers coffee-dipped ladyfingers with mascarpone, whipped cream and soft Spanish almond turrón. Serve in glasses after at least four hours in the fridge.
turron.notes: Use soft almond turrón, Jijona style, not hard white nougat. No raw egg is added, but the biscuits and turrón may contain cooked egg, so this is not egg-allergy safe. Contains milk, almonds and wheat. Use pasteurised dairy; refrigerate covered at 4 °C or below for up to 2 days. Decaffeinated coffee works. This editorial formulation has not been physically kitchen-tested.
ingredients: soft Spanish almond turrón, Jijona style
steps: Prepare coffee and glasses
Make 180 ml unsweetened coffee and let it cool completely. Arrange six 200 ml glasses on a tray.
Crumble the turrón
Finely crumble 150 g soft almond turrón. Reserve 20 g for finishing and put the remaining 130 g in a bowl.
Mix the nougat cream
Add 250 g mascarpone to the bowl. Beat briefly on low speed until evenly mixed; do not overbeat.
Fold in whipped cream
Whip 200 g cold cream to soft peaks and gently fold into the mascarpone and turrón.
Make the first layer
Break 120 g ladyfingers to fit the glasses. Quickly dip half in the cold coffee and place in the bottoms without soaking.
Alternate the layers
Add half the cream. Repeat with the remaining dipped biscuits and finish with the remaining cream. You may not need all the coffee.
Chill to set
Cover the glasses without touching the cream and refrigerate for at least 4 hours.
Finish before serving
Sift 8 g cocoa over the six glasses and scatter over the reserved 20 g turrón. Serve cold and keep remaining portions refrigerated.
faq: Is this egg-free?
No raw egg is added, but the biscuits and some turrón contain cooked egg. Check labels for allergies.
Which turrón should I use?
Soft Spanish almond turrón, Jijona style, which crumbles easily and blends into mascarpone.
How long should it chill?
At least 4 hours. Make it the day before and add the cocoa and final turrón just before serving.

datiles.title: Goat cheese stuffed dates wrapped in bacon
datiles.summary: Large Medjool dates are filled with soft goat cheese and wrapped in thin bacon. Roast until golden, then finish with a restrained drizzle of chilli honey.
datiles.notes: Use large Medjool dates, thin bacon and pasteurised goat cheese. Remove every stone and all cocktail sticks before eating. Contains milk. Nutrition includes all the bacon and honey without subtracting fat left in the tray, so the estimate may be high. Refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours for up to 3 days and reheat until hot throughout.
ingredients: large Medjool dates, weighed after pitting
thin bacon, six rashers cut in half
steps: Prepare the tray
Heat the conventional oven to 200 °C. Put an oven-safe wire rack over a rimmed tray to catch the fat.
Pit the dates
Slit twelve large Medjool dates lengthways and remove the stones without separating the halves. Aim for about 288 g pitted fruit.
Add the cheese
Divide 90 g goat cheese between the dates, about 7–8 g each. Close gently without squeezing out the filling.
Wrap with bacon
Cut six thin bacon rashers in half to make twelve strips. Wrap one around each date.
Secure and arrange
Secure each with a cocktail stick. Arrange on the rack seam-side down, with space between them.
Roast and turn
Bake for 20–25 minutes, carefully turning halfway, until the bacon is golden and fully cooked. Adjust for thickness and follow the bacon packet cooking instructions.
Add chilli honey
Mix 15 g honey with 0.5 g dried chilli. Rest the dates for 5 minutes out of the oven, then drizzle a small amount over each.
Serve the bites
Serve two warm dates per person on a cream platter. Warn guests about the sticks and remove them before eating; the filling retains heat.
faq: Can I prepare them ahead?
Yes. Assemble up to 12 hours ahead and keep covered in the fridge. Bake before serving.
Which cheese works?
Soft pasteurised goat cheese. Cream cheese also works but changes flavour and nutrition.
Can I leave out the chilli?
Yes. Use plain honey or omit the glaze. The published estimate includes 15 g honey and the chilli.
